query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing that inherits microstructural lamellae will improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys by reducing microcracking and enhancing grain boundary cohesion.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries
generation.intervention: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing with inheritance of microstructural lamellae
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary cohesion and reduced microcracking
generation.mechanism: Enhanced strength-ductility synergy through designed microstructural architectures
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in tensile strength and 30% increase in tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline
generation.boundary: Processing temperatures between 800°C and 1000°C, strain rates between 10^-3 s^-1 and 10^-1 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The exact processing parameters and resulting microstructural features may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing history

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of specimens with tailored thermo-mechanical processing and unmodified lamellar-colony microstructure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tailored thermo-mechanical processing does not result in a significant improvement (less than 10% increase) in both tensile strength and tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, the hypothesis is falsified
